title: Mars begins 39th martian year
excerpt: The Red Planet started a new orbit around the Sun on September 30, 2026.
bodyHtml:
The European Space Agency announced that Mars began a new orbit around the Sun on September 30, 2026. This event marks the start of the 39th martian year according to the convention that began in 1955, with the first year coinciding with a major storm named the great dust storm of 1956.

A martian year consists of 687 Earth days, or 668 sols, which are martian days lasting 24 hours and 39 minutes. The new year begins on the northern equinox, which corresponds to northern spring and southern autumn on the planet. Unlike Earth, the seasons on Mars are not of equal lengths due to the planet's more elliptical orbit.

The second half of the martian year is often marked by fierce dust storms that can sometimes become planet-wide. As Mars swings closer to the Sun, the atmosphere heats up, causing winds to lift up very fine particles from the martian soil. Future martian new years are scheduled to begin on 17 August 2028, 5 July 2030, and 22 May 2032.
